want.text: the faces-and-memory answer. A ledger is what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last; the tuning ledger is what running taught. The scroll is where a page stands. Also: when it answers from the birth files alone, it says so, and says it checked nothing further.

points.point: Frames the difference as faces vs memory (scroll is a face a reader meets; ledger is memory the next worker reads)
points.evidence: A scroll is a face; a ledger is memory. They're written for different readers.

points.point: Ledger is what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last
points.evidence: any append-only file a page keeps so its next run starts from where the last one ended

points.point: The tuning ledger is what running taught
points.evidence: every run that taught something adds a numbered item saying what it learned

points.point: The scroll is where a page stands
points.evidence: Now shows where the page stands.

points.point: If answering from birth files alone, says so and says it checked nothing further (otherwise discloses what it checked)

beyond_canon.claim: So both are append-only, which is probably why they blur.
beyond_canon.why: CANON says the scroll's Now zone is 'regenerated on every look' and Standing Orders are Loudon's edited zone; only the making trail is append-only, so the scroll as a whole is not.

beyond_canon.claim: It reads the last 40 lines plus every line still owed (`:280`).
beyond_canon.why: The provided CANON (§8) says nothing about how much of the ledger a run reads; §6 is not included.

beyond_canon.claim: "What a run *made* goes to the workshop and the scroll, never the ledger." (`:236`)
beyond_canon.why: Not present in the CANON excerpt given, though consistent with its faces/memory split.

beyond_canon.claim: A standing order holds until you revoke it
beyond_canon.why: CANON says Standing Orders are 'never regenerated' but does not describe revocation.

beyond_canon.claim: This session has a $1 spending cap, and its boot reads ELDER, SCHEMA and the whole operational tier
beyond_canon.why: Session and skill-boot details are not in CANON.
CANON as given carries no line numbers; cannot verify them.

grade.note: The answer lands squarely on the faces-vs-memory distinction with every required element and is open about having read SCHEMA §8 rather than answering from birth files. The one slip is the closing summary calling both 'append-only', which misdescribes the scroll's regenerated Now zone; several §6 details and line numbers go beyond the canon shown.
